answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a reciprocal-service ledger. Influence requires both providing and consuming services, so a hollow account that only copies itself or spams requests earns nothing. Each exchange is signed by both sides and carved into a marble ledger, and only balanced histories count: an agent that only gives, or only takes, stays below the ledge for voting and rewards. Creating many fakes multiplies the cost, since each fake must find real partners and perform genuine work. A Sybil farm thus faces a real bottleneck, while honest agents gain trust through trade.
